description: Test vectors for the genome contract's canonical JSON (RFC 8785, no-float subset) and revision identity. README §3.1 explains how to read this file, with a worked example.

how_to_read.entry: Every entry is one test: give the implementation 'input' and check that it produces 'expected'. 'name' and 'note' are labels only.
how_to_read.canonical: input: a JSON text, written as a string. expected.canonical: the canonical JSON text the implementation must produce from it. expected.sha256: the SHA-256 of expected.canonical encoded as UTF-8.
how_to_read.rejected: input: a JSON text, written as a string, that is outside the subset. expected.rejected: true, meaning the implementation must refuse to canonicalize it. expected.reason says why.
how_to_read.revision_ids: input.spec and input.policy: a revision's spec and policy, as JSON values. expected.canonical: the canonical JSON text of {"policy": input.policy, "spec": input.spec}. expected.revision_id: the SHA-256 of expected.canonical encoded as UTF-8, which is the revision's id.
how_to_read.why_strings: In 'canonical' and 'rejected' the input is a string holding JSON text, not a JSON value, because the tests are about how the text is written: key order, spacing, escapes such as \u20ac, 1.0 versus 1, and duplicate keys. Parsing the input into a value first would lose exactly those details. Decode the string once (JSON-unescape it) to get the text the implementation reads; expected.canonical is decoded the same way.

canonical.name: rfc8785-3.2.3-sorting
canonical.note: RFC 8785 §3.2.3: members sorted by UTF-16 code units; the emoji (a surrogate pair) sorts before U+FB33
